newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Racal profits drop, aims for overhaul.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Racal profits drop, aims for overhaul.

text.p: Racal Electronics Plc announced a sharp drop in profits on Tuesday and launched a drive to increase shareholder value, focusing on telecommunications, data products and defence electronics.

Pretax profits fell to 40.4 million pounds ($66 million) for the year to March 31 from 70.4 million pounds last year, after hefty charges of 29 million pounds for restructuring its Data Products division.
But sales were up 142 million pounds at 1.138 billion pounds and the final dividend of 3.9 pence maintained the total dividend payout at six pence a share for the year.
Racal shares bounced 6-1/2 pence a share to 240 after the news but had slipped back to 234 pence by 1020 GMT as an analysts' meeting with the firm got underway on details of the strategic review.
Racal has been under pressure to come up with a new strategy following a 30 percent slump in the share price in the last year and a series of profit warnings.
Recent press speculation has suggested that Racal's veteran chairman Sir Ernest Harrison would demerge the group or at least reshape it through a series of disposals, mergers and alliances.

In the event the company said in its results statement on Tuesday only that it had called in mergers and acquisition advisers to help it to "maximise shareholder value" and refocus the group on the three principal businesses.
But it also said it expected to cut nearly 1,000 jobs from its worldwide workforce of 15,000 in the current year.

The company warned the job cuts meant there would be "a significant increase" in the impact of reorganisation costs on operating profits in the current year, although pre-tax profits would be up on the result just reported.

However it said in the statement that continuing losses in its Radio Communications division, margin pressure in Telecommunications Services and the costs of rationalisation would "adversely impact" the first-half result.

Following a strategic review, the company said it would work to concentrate the business on three principal activities: "Telecommunications Services and Data Products operating in dynamic markets, and Defence Electronics with growth opportunities."

Racal said its Data Products business was now in shape following a fundamental restructuring last year to tackle what it sees as a fast growing market for multimedia communications systems, expanding at 25 percent a year.
"New products to meet these requirements are being introduced and the initial reaction from industry analysts and customers has been positive," the company said in its results statement.
